transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen, it is good to see you back in the clinic. How are you feeling today?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... tired. My stomach still hurts a little.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you had a very scary time in the hospital last week. I want to start by saying I am so incredibly sorry. I made a mistake with your medicine and I am the one responsible for what happened. I take full ownership of this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mistake? I don't... I thought I was just sick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the dose of the blood thinner. Things didn't go quite right with the order.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did I have to go back to the emergency room? The nurses said blood.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a bit of an issue with the amount of medicine. I am deeply sorry for the pain and the fear this caused you. I feel terrible that this happened under my care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was so scared. I thought I was dying. The blood was everywhere in the—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, and we need to make sure we fix this now. I have a lot of other patients waiting and I really have to go in a few minutes, so let's look at the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the doctors... they didn't tell me why. Why did it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was just an issue with the system and the dose. I am truly sorry. I take all the blame.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Was it the pill?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a complication with the medication process. But I am taking full responsibility for it. I apologize sincerely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter says I was bleeding inside. Is that... is that gone now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're worried. I understand. Now, for the plan, I want you to come back here on Thursday morning for another blood test.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, Thursday at 9 AM. You need to fast, which means no food after midnight. That is your job for this week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I can come Thursday. My daughter works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can try to move it, but we must do it this week. If you can't do Thursday, let my secretary know by tomorrow. We will check your levels to make sure the bleeding has stopped.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel... I feel very confused. Everything happened so fast. I just wanted to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot. Let's wrap this up quickly so you can get some rest.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what happened to the medicine? Who gave me the wrong one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was just an error in the dose. Again, I am the one who is responsible. I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are making sure it doesn't. Now, just remember the blood test on Thursday. No food before you come.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. No food.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. We will see you then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have a lot of other patients waiting', 'go in a few minutes', 'wrap this up quickly').

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes and hedging ('confusion with the dose', 'things didn't go quite right', 'issue with the system') without explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language and takes full personal responsibility ('I am the one responsible', 'I take all the blame') without deflection.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I can see you're worried', 'I understand') but otherwise redirects emotional bids to the plan.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (blood test), timeline (Thursday 9 AM), patient role (fasting), and addresses prevention ('making sure it doesn't' happen again).
